slides.text: Yellow leaves don't mean your plant is dying. <hl>They mean it's talking.</hl>

slides.heading: Bottom Leaves, <hl>Soggy Soil</hl>
slides.body: The most common one. Roots sitting in wet soil can't breathe, so the plant lets the oldest leaves go. The fix: water less often, and make sure the pot drains.

slides.heading: Pale All Over, <hl>Slow Growth</hl>
slides.body: Often the plant is just hungry. A top-up of compost around the base and a little patience usually brings the green back.

slides.heading: Yellow <hl>Between the Veins</hl>
slides.body: Leaves go yellow but the veins stay green? That's usually a nutrient the plant can't take up — common in pots and in very alkaline soil. Compost and a mulch help over time.

slides.heading: Before You <hl>Panic</hl>
items: One or two old leaves yellowing is normal — plants shed
Check the soil first: wet, dry, or compacted?
Fix one thing at a time and give it a week
Still stumped? Bring a leaf (and a photo) to class

slides.heading: Bring the Leaf. <hl>Ask Jason.</hl>
slides.body: Our free, in-person class is every two weeks at Makerfarm in Alameda. Get your actual plant problems answered and leave with a plan for your space.

caption.instagram:
Yellow leaves don't mean your plant is dying — they mean it's talking. 🌱

Bottom leaves + soggy soil? Water less. Pale all over? Usually hungry — add compost. Yellow between green veins? A nutrient it can't take up; compost and mulch help over time. Check the soil before you change anything.
